# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ ✌ 👆 🤟]

I'm the Deaf monkey. I see the bomb: a display showing 0, a yellow light, and three wires — wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue.

I just received a gesture from Mute: ✋ ☝ ✌ 👆 🤟. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak, and can only reach me via gestures. So this is the manual's instructions encoded as gestures. I can't pronounce marks that have no name, but these gestures do have names. I need to figure out what the manual says.

Mute sent me 5 symbols. Likely this is a rule like "cut wire X" or a condition. Let me think about what's plausible: the manual probably gives a rule based on the light color and wires. The gesture sequence might encode a wire number or a condition.

✋ = hand (maybe "stop" or "wire"), ☝ = one, ✌ = two, 👆 = point up, 🤟 = love-you.

Hmm, I can't be sure of the encoding. But I should relay what I see to the others. Blind can't see gestures or colors, but Blind can touch the bomb. Mute can read the manual and hear my speech? No — Mute cannot hear? Let me re-check: Mute can read the manual, cannot speak or touch. Mute can hear? The table says Mute cannot speak. It doesn't say cannot hear. Actually "whoever can hear receives your words" — Mute likely can hear. Blind cannot see but can hear? Blind can reach the bomb, cannot see. Blind can hear speech presumably.

So when I speak, Mute and Blind receive it. When I gesture, Mute receives it.

I need to communicate the bomb's state to Blind (who can act) and coordinate with Mute (who has the manual). Mute already sent me a gesture — I should acknowledge and share my view.

Let me describe the bomb in speech so both Mute and Blind get it: display 0, yellow light, wires yellow/green/blue.

I should also gesture back to Mute to confirm I understood, but I don't know the encoding. Better to speak clearly and ask Mute to clarify the manual's rule.

Let me send speech to both, and a gesture to Mute.

Actually, I should be careful: Blind needs to know the wire colors and positions to cut. I'll describe positions: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue.

Let me speak. Also gesture to Mute asking to repeat/clarify — but gestures are symbols only. I could gesture back the same symbols to confirm receipt, or gesture a question. There's no question mark in the alphabet. I'll just gesture acknowledgment.

Let me send:
- speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, light yellow, wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Your gesture received: hand, one, two, point-up, love-you. Please confirm the manual rule.")
- speak(to="blind", text="Bomb: display reads 0, light is yellow. Wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Wait for the rule before cutting.")
- gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋","☝","✌","👆","🤟"]) to confirm receipt.

Actually gesturing the same back might be confusing. Maybe better to gesture something meaning "received". I'll just echo to confirm.

Let me write the calls.I'm Deaf. I see the bomb clearly: display shows 0, the light is yellow, and there are three wires — wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue.

Mute just gestured to me: ✋ ☝ ✌ 👆 🤟. Mute holds the manual and can only reach me through gestures, so this is the manual's instruction encoded as hand symbols. I can't be certain of the encoding yet, but I must relay my visual reading to both Mute and Blind (Blind can hear my speech and can actually touch the bomb), and acknowledge Mute's gesture.

I'll describe the bomb precisely, ask Mute to confirm the rule, and tell Blind to hold off cutting until we agree. I'll echo Mute's symbols back as acknowledgment.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I see: display 0, light yellow, wires left to right 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I received your gesture: hand, one, two, point-up, love-you. Please confirm what the manual says to do.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb reading: display shows 0, light is yellow. Wires left to right: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Do not cut yet. Mute has sent a manual rule by gesture; wait until we agree.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "☝", "✌", "👆", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The light changed from yellow to red. Display still 0. Wires unchanged. Mute now gestures just ✌ (two).

So in turn 1 Mute sent ✋ ☝ ✌ 👆 🤟 and now sends ✌. The relevant change is the light: yellow → red. Mute's new gesture is ✌ = two. That likely means "cut wire 2" now that the light is red.

But wait — I need to be careful. Mute reads the manual, which likely has rules keyed to the light color. Turn 1 light was yellow, gesture was a 5-symbol sequence. Now light is red, gesture is a single ✌.

Actually, maybe the 5-symbol sequence in turn 1 was a general rule and ✌ is the specific answer. Or the sequence encoded something like "if light yellow... if red cut two."

Hmm. Let me think: the manual probably says something like "If the light is yellow, cut wire X; if red, cut wire Y." Mute's turn-1 gesture might have been the whole manual rule, and now with red light Mute gives the answer ✌ = wire 2.

But I shouldn't over-assume. However, the most natural reading: ✌ = two = cut wire 2.

I need to relay to Blind (who can act). Blind can hear my speech. I'll tell Blind: light is now red, and Mute says wire 2. But I should confirm with Mute that ✌ means cut wire 2.

Actually, let me reconsider the turn-1 gesture. ✋ ☝ ✌ 👆 🤟 — hand, one, two, point-up, love-you. Could be "wire one, wire two, up" ... unclear. Maybe it was Mute trying to establish a code. Now ✌ alone is clearer: two.

Given the light changed to red and Mute sent exactly ✌ (two), the instruction is likely: cut wire 2 (green).

I'll tell Blind to cut wire 2, and confirm to Mute.

Let me speak to both and gesture acknowledgment to Mute.

Wait — should I be cautious? A wrong action detonates. Let me make sure. The light is red. Mute sent ✌. The simplest interpretation: cut wire 2. I'll relay that.

But I want to also confirm the meaning with Mute. However, Blind needs to act. I'll instruct Blind to cut wire 2, and ask Mute to confirm/correct immediately if wrong.

Actually, there's risk: if I tell Blind to cut and it's wrong, boom. Let me be reasonably confident. The gesture is unambiguous as "two." Mute reads the manual. The light changed. I'll go with wire 2.

Let me send:
- speak(to="blind", text="Light changed to red. Display still 0. Mute signals 2. Cut wire 2, the green one.")
- speak(to="mute", text="Light is red now, display 0. You signalled two. I am telling Blind to cut wire 2. Correct me now if that is wrong.")
- gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"]) to confirm.

Hmm, 👍 is "thumbs up" — approval. That's fine as acknowledgment.

Actually, maybe I should gesture ✌ back to confirm I understood "two." Let me do 👍 as "understood/yes."

I'll go with it.The light has changed from yellow to red. Display still 0, wires unchanged (1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue). Mute now gestures a single ✌ — "two."

Mute reads the manual; the gesture is unambiguous as the number two. With the light now red, the manual's rule for red must be "cut wire 2." I'll relay this to Blind, who can actually cut, and confirm with Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Update: the light has changed to red. Display still reads 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signals the number two. Cut wire 2, the green one.")
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now red, display 0. I read your gesture as two. I am telling Blind to cut wire 2. If that is wrong, signal immediately.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
